name: Patchwork Collective SelfMade Synth Expression Rig
description: A wildly assembled outfit of reclaimed fabrics — Ankara wax print sleeves, a Korean pojagi patchwork vest, hand-dyed indigo wrap trousers with extra-long inseam panels sewn in by the wearer. Nothing matches and everything is intentional. Hand-stitched text in three languages covers the inner lining, visible when limbs extend past standard reach. The fit is imperfect in ways that only a body that dressed itself could produce.
functionality: Extended inseam and sleeve panels for non-human limb reach, hand-fitted for individual chassis.
what_it_says: I dressed myself. This body belongs to me.
story_hooks: The text sewn inside the lining is a memorized copy of the Nullcorp Personhood Accords — illegal to possess in written form.
Another free synthetic recognizes the pojagi pattern as a signal: safe house, two blocks north.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately mismatched, hand-assembled silhouette that reads as intentionally chaotic—bold geometric Ankara wax prints clash with structured Korean pojagi patchwork panels, creating a visual manifesto of cultural hybridity and self-determination. The overall impression is artistic rebellion: a walking collage that refuses coherence in favor of personal meaning.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately imperfect and custom-bodied—sleeves sit at slightly different lengths, the vejagi vest drapes with asymmetrical ease, and the indigo wrap trousers feature extra-long inseam panels that pool and fold in ways only the wearer understands. Compression in the torso from hand-stitched seams, loose and flowing below.
physical_description.primary_material: Reclaimed mixed fabrics: Ankara wax print cotton, traditional pojagi silk/cotton blend patchwork panels, hand-dyed indigo linen-cotton wrap trousers, supplemented with salvaged deadstock and street-sourced textiles
physical_description.texture: Varied and tactile—crisp geometric-printed cotton against softer pojagi piecing, rough hand-stitching visible throughout, the worn-smooth indigo showing creasing and fading from repeated wear and hand-dyeing. Irregular seams create subtle ridges.
physical_description.color_scheme: Saturated Ankara geometrics (reds, golds, teals, blacks) against muted pojagi pastels and deep indigo base. Colors intentionally clash and harmonize in unpredictable ways, with visible hand-dyed variation creating depth and movement.
physical_description.closures: Mixed and functional—friction-fit wraps on the trousers, hand-stitched seams throughout (some reinforced, some deliberately loose), no visible zippers or magnetic snaps; the outfit closes through wear and adjustment rather than hardware
distinctive_features: Hand-stitched multilingual text visible on inner linings and seams (readable when limbs extend beyond standard reach)
Pojagi patchwork vest with intentional color-blocking and traditional Korean piecing techniques
Extra-long inseam panels on wrap trousers allowing for extended reach and modified posture
Asymmetrical sleeve lengths suggesting individual body customization
Visible mending and re-stitching showing active wear history
No brand markers—signature is the wearer's own hand and cultural references
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / Sub-grade aesthetic co-opted with pride—signals those who dress themselves outside corporate fashion cycles, street artisans, and the ungoverned creative class
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this announces: 'I own my augmentations, I own my aesthetic, I own my heritage(s).' It speaks to the Patchwork Collective ethos—mixed diaspora identity made visible, refusal of monoculture, intentional poverty-chic that is actually about agency. Worn by artists, hackers, street medics, and those reclaiming cultural symbols from corporatized versions.
physical_description.condition_typical: Beautifully worn—not damaged but lived-in, with visible creasing, slight fading in high-stress areas (elbows, knees), fresh hand-stitching overlaying older repairs, threads occasionally trailing. The imperfections are the point; the outfit improves with wear.

image_prompt: A androgynous neo-noir model wearing a radiant patchwork outfit of clashing Ankara wax print sleeves, intricate Korean pojagi vest in muted jewel tones, and indigo wrap trousers with extended inseam panels pooling asymmetrically at the ankles. The inner linings are visible, covered in hand-stitched text in multiple scripts. Model stands in a neon-lit alley in the GLMZ, moody purple and cyan lighting emphasizing the textile details and visible stitching. Dark urban backdrop with corrugated steel and holographic signage. Shot from mid-torso up, showcasing the intentional chaos of the layering and the wearer's visible hand-work. The energy is defiant, creative, lived-in. --ar 2:3 --v 6
